transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. What brings you in today?

After losing a job opportunity I was really counting on, I feel like I’ve been reacting badly to everything. I just can’t seem to cope with what’s happening in my life right now and feel completely thrown off course.
How long have you been feeling this way, and were there any other major stressful events around the time you lost the job opportunity?

It’s been about two months now, starting just a few weeks after I found out the nonprofit job fell through. Around that same time, everything hit me at once because my student loan payments were coming due and my apartment lease was up for renewal.
Have your symptoms improved at all since the stressful events, like the job loss or housing and financial issues, began to settle, or have they continued without relief?

No, they haven't improved because none of those situations have actually settled yet—everything is still completely up in the air. I've been feeling this way without any relief for the past two months. I really think I'll only start to feel better once I can get these life circumstances sorted out.
Besides feeling overwhelmed, have you been experiencing persistent sadness, anxiety, or difficulty sleeping that goes beyond just reacting to these stressors?

Honestly, my feelings of sadness and anxiety—like crying or having my chest tighten over a simple email—are completely tied to this job situation and its fallout. I was doing totally fine before this happened two months ago. It really feels like a reaction to everything being so up in the air right now rather than some separate, long-standing issue.
